We need a CloudFormation template that creates the IAM roles and user group required for AWS Service Catalog launch constraints, specifically covering an end-user IAM stack plus launch constraint roles for EC2-VPC, EMR, RDS, and S3 product templates, using nested stacks that pull the IAM templates from a repository root URL parameter, with a default value pointing to the standard AWS Service Catalog reference architectures S3 location, and after deployment the stack should expose the generated group and launch role references as outputs so they can be easily consumed by other stacks when configuring Service Catalog launch constraints.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a self-service Cognito user pool for testing JWT authentication flows with an AgentCore Gateway and MCP server, where users can sign up using their email address and verify themselves without any admin intervention by enabling self-service signup with email verification, and the pool should include a hosted UI domain for signup and login pages, a resource server with identifier "api" and custom scopes named "mcp" and "gateway", a public web client that supports authorization code with PKCE along with explicit auth flows for USER_PASSWORD_AUTH and USER_SRP_AUTH for programmatic testing with token validity set to 60 minutes for access and ID tokens and 30 days for refresh tokens, and two separate machine-to-machine clients that use the client credentials grant with the appropriate custom scopes for gateway and MCP server authentication, each with a generated client secret and token validity of 60 minutes for access and ID tokens and 1 day for refresh tokens, and the template should accept comma-delimited parameters for callback and logout URLs with sensible localhost defaults.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a self-contained Kinesis Firehose delivery stream configured for DirectPut delivery, which compresses incoming data using GZIP and buffers it for up to 900 seconds or 128 MB before writing to a newly provisioned S3 bucket under a "raw/MyKinesisFirehose/" prefix; the stack must also create that S3 bucket, a dedicated CloudWatch log group with a 14-day retention policy and a log stream named "firehose" to capture delivery stream logs, an IAM role that allows the Firehose service to assume it and grants permissions for S3 PutObject, GetObject, AbortMultipartUpload, GetBucketLocation, ListBucket, and ListBucketMultipartUploads on the target bucket and its prefix path as well as full CloudWatch Logs access on the created log group, and a CloudWatch alarm that monitors the DeliveryToS3.DataFreshness metric every 60 seconds with a threshold of 1800 seconds and treats missing data as not breaching.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates shared IAM roles and activates third-party CloudFormation resource types to enable provisioning of an EKS cluster and Helm releases via CloudFormation, using parameters for an environment alias, environment ID, an optional permissions boundary ARN, and an optional S3 bucket name for node access to objects; the template should include an execution role that allows Lambda and CloudFormation services to assume it with permissions to manage the EKS cluster and perform resource logging, an access role for EC2 instances that includes managed policies for Systems Manager and CloudWatch and allows reading from the specified S3 bucket, and two type activations for the AWSQS-Kubernetes-Helm and AWSQS-EKS-Cluster resource types, with logging configured for both.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway infrastructure for MCP (Model Context Protocol) integration with an AI agent used for protein variant effect prediction, where the template must be fully self-contained and create all necessary resources including a Lambda function for invoking predictions and retrieving results, a Cognito user pool with client and domain for JWT authorization with the gateway's discovery URL and client ID stored in SSM Parameter Store, an IAM role assumed by the bedrock-agentcore.amazonaws.com service with permissions to invoke the Lambda function and store its ARN in SSM Parameter Store, the gateway itself with a custom JWT authorizer referencing those Cognito SSM parameters, a gateway target connecting to the Lambda with MCP tool schema defining invoke_endpoint and get_results operations, and the gateway role ARN also stored in SSM Parameter Store, with the project name defaulting to "protein-engineering", gateway description defaulting to "AgentCore Gateway for protein engineering agent with MCP integration", and gateway name either auto-generated from the project name or explicitly provided.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates an AWS App Runner service for a multi-tenant QuickSight dashboard application, provisioning a new ECR repository and container image within the same account and region, with auto-deployments enabled and a health check at the /status path on port 8080, while also creating IAM roles: a build role with permissions to access ECR (including GetAuthorizationToken and image pull operations) and a task role with permissions to call Directory Service and QuickSight APIs (such as CreateNamespace, CreateDataSet, RegisterUser, and related actions) to support tenant provisioning, and configuring the App Runner service with runtime environment variables including ALLOW_IP_RANGE set to 0.0.0.0/0, the AWS region and account ID, a dummy email placeholder, an admin user name, and template, dataset, datasource, database, table, and filter column identifiers for the QuickSight integration, with the template being fully self-contained and outputting the generated image URI and the App Runner service URL.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a regional Web Application Firewall for an Application Load Balancer, using a customizable stack prefix parameter that defaults to "sera" and must be 3-21 lowercase characters starting with a letter, where the WAF allows all traffic by default and includes a general rate limit rule blocking IPs that exceed 2000 requests per 5 minutes, a stricter rate limit rule blocking IPs that exceed 1000 requests per 5 minutes for URI paths containing "/api/", and enables the AWS managed rule groups for common threats, known bad inputs, SQL injection, Linux operating system protection, and IP reputation monitoring with no excluded rules, and the template must provision a new Application Load Balancer and a new KMS key within the same stack, associate the WAF with that ALB, and send all WAF logs to a CloudWatch log group with 10-year retention encrypted using the newly created KMS key, with a logging filter that only keeps log entries where the action was COUNT.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a self-contained AWS Cognito authentication infrastructure for an application called "nih-grants", including a user pool with multi-factor authentication enabled and advanced security mode enforced, an identity pool that supports both authenticated and unauthenticated identities (with unauthenticated access disabled by default), and two app clients (one for web and one for general use) with a 30-day refresh token validity. We need a CloudFormation template that creates an AWS Backup infrastructure to automatically back up all resources tagged with the key "backup" and values "daily", "weekly", and "monthly", with daily backups running each day at 5 AM UTC and retaining for 14 days, weekly backups each Sunday at 5 AM UTC retaining for 56 days, and monthly backups on the first day of each month at 5 AM UTC retaining for 365 days; the template should include separate encrypted backup vaults for each schedule, a KMS key with rotation enabled, an IAM service role for AWS Backup, and tag-based backup selections that use the specified tags, as well as provision Service Catalog TagOption key-value pairs for the backup tag values to integrate with Service Catalog portfolios and products, and all resources must be self-contained within the stack.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates security groups for a video streaming application stack consisting of Redis, server, origin, and proxy components, using a VPC imported from a stack named 'video-streaming-vpc' by default, with the Redis security group allowing all traffic from the origin and server container security groups, the server container security group allowing all traffic from its own load balancer, the proxy container, the origin container, and itself as well as TCP on ports 1935 and 8000 from anywhere, the server load balancer security group allowing TCP on port 1935 from anywhere, the origin load balancer security group allowing TCP on ports 80 and 443 from anywhere, the origin container security group allowing TCP on port 80 only from its load balancer, and the proxy container security group allowing TCP on ports 1935, 3000, 8080, 80, and 443 from anywhere, and exporting each security group for use by other stacks.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a SageMaker notebook instance for RAPIDS AI development, including an IAM role with the AmazonSageMakerFullAccess managed policy, a lifecycle configuration that installs a RAPIDS AI conda environment and registers a Jupyter kernel on notebook creation and start, and a GPU-enabled notebook instance of type ml.p3.2xlarge with 50 GB of storage, named "rapidsai", and configured to clone the default repository from https://github.com/rapidsai/notebooks.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates its own EKS cluster, two private subnets in the first two available availability zones, and the required security groups (an EMR cluster security group and an EMR Celeborn access security group) so that the entire environment is self-contained, then provisions managed node groups for EMR on EKS Spark workloads: a general node group for system pods with m5.xlarge instances, min/desired size of 2 and max of 3, and a Spark node group for executor pods with memory-optimized r5.2xlarge instances, min/desired size of 3 and max of 6, both on-demand using Amazon Linux 2023 x86_64 standard AMI with 50 GB disk and attaching a launch template that references the newly created security groups, along with an IAM role for the node groups containing the AmazonEKSWorkerNodePolicy, AmazonEKS_CNI_Policy, AmazonEC2ContainerRegistryReadOnly, and AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore policies, and a separate IAM role for the EBS CSI driver with the AmazonEBSCSIDriverPolicy to be used later for IRSA (without deploying the addon), with all instance types, scaling sizes, and a project name parameter defaulting to "emr-celeborn-demo" parameterized, and exporting the two node group names and the CSI driver role name as stack outputs.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a self-contained SLO monitoring dashboard and associated CloudWatch alarms for an event-driven pipeline pattern based on FSx for ONTAP, with the following objectives: the template must define four SLO alarms—EventIngestionLatency (P99 threshold of 5 seconds), ProcessingSuccessRate (average threshold of 99.5%), FPolicyReconnectTime (maximum threshold of 30 seconds), and ReplayCompletionTime (maximum threshold of 5 minutes)—each evaluated over three consecutive 5-minute periods with missing data treated as not breaching, and all alarms should optionally forward to an SNS topic if an ARN is provided, but the template must create all other resources itself without relying on pre-existing components. The entire dashboard and alarm set should only be deployed when an explicit enable flag is set to true (defaulting to false), using a project prefix defaulting to "fsxn-s3ap", a metric namespace defaulting to "FSxN-S3AP-Patterns", and a canary metric namespace defaulting to "FSxN-S3AP-Patterns/Canary", while the region should default to us-east-1 and all thresholds must be configurable via parameters.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates monthly COST budgets for our key security and monitoring services, including AWS Config, CloudWatch, GuardDuty, Inspector, Security Hub, and S3 for security logs, with budget limits of $10,000 for Config and CloudWatch and $1,000 for the remaining services; each budget must be of type COST with a MONTHLY time unit, a defined time period that starts in the past and extends to a distant end date, and the required cost type settings that include recurring, subscription, other-subscription, and upfront charges while excluding credits, discounts, refunds, support, and tax, and the budgets must be retained even if the stack is deleted.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates an AWS App Mesh environment for testing mutual TLS communication between services, including a mesh, a virtual gateway, a virtual service, a gateway route, and a virtual node, where the virtual gateway and virtual node are configured with TLS settings based on a parameter that can be set to no-tls, 1way-tls, or mtls, the virtual service points to the virtual node using a configurable service domain, and all resources use configurable environment name and mesh name, with the template requiring pre-existing ACM PCA certificate authority ARNs imported via cross-stack references (e.g., `${EnvironmentName}:AcmPcaColorTellerRootCAArn` and `${EnvironmentName}:AcmPcaColorTellerEndpointCertArn`) that must be available in the same account and region.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a set of self-contained Step Functions state machines for testing cross-workflow orchestration, including an EXPRESS state machine that simply succeeds, a STANDARD state machine that uses a synchronous start execution task to invoke the first state machine with definition substitutions, and two additional STANDARD state machines that are also simple succeed states but share a common IAM role; the template must also create the necessary IAM roles with trust policies for Step Functions and attach managed policies that grant the trigger state machine's role permissions to start, stop, and describe executions of the destination state machine, as well as manage EventBridge rules, while the destination state machine's role should have a basic Lambda invocation policy, and all resources should be tagged with a stateMachine:createdBy tag set to SAM.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates an ECS service with service discovery and CPU-based autoscaling, importing the ECS cluster name, private service discovery namespace ID, and autoscaling IAM role ARN from another stack via cross-stack references, using configurable parameters for environment name (default 'production'), service name (default 'nginx'), Docker image URL (default 'nginx'), container port (default 80), CPU and memory units (default 256 and 512), desired count (default 2), and an optional IAM role ARN for the task's containers; the template must create a CloudWatch Logs log group, an ECS task definition, a private service discovery service with an SRV DNS record (TTL of 10 seconds) and a custom health check with a failure threshold of 1, an ECS service registered in that discovery service with a deployment configuration of 200% maximum and 75% minimum healthy percent, and an Application Auto Scaling scalable target with a minimum capacity of 2 and maximum capacity of 10, then set up step scaling policies with a 60-second cooldown—a scale-down step that reduces desired count by one when average CPU utilization drops to 20% or below, and a scale-up policy that increases desired count by one, two, or three depending on how much CPU exceeds 70%—both triggered by CloudWatch alarms that evaluate average CPU usage every 60 seconds.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a self-contained AWS Fault Injection Simulator experiment template for chaos engineering across multiple regions, designed to disrupt cross-region network connectivity by targeting transit gateways and subnets, and to pause replication for S3 buckets and DynamoDB global tables, all targeting resources tagged with ChaosAllowed set to true, with a configurable experiment duration defaulting to 20 minutes and a target region defaulting to us-east-1, and including a CloudWatch log group encrypted with a new KMS key for experiment logs with a retention period of 7 days, with the experiment template configured to have stop conditions set to none and empty target resolution mode set to skip, all within a single stack that provisions a new IAM role with multiple managed policies attached to allow the FIS service to perform the disruptions.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a Docker-based worker service for a voting application, running on AWS Fargate, that is self-contained within the environment and connects to both a MongoDB instance and a Redis endpoint, where the MongoDB URI is provided as a template parameter and the Redis endpoint is imported from the environment’s shared stack, with the service configured to run two initial copies of the task, each receiving 1024 CPU units and 2048 MB of memory, and the template includes automatic scaling based on CPU utilization so that when the average CPU drops to 20 percent or below the service scales down by one task, and when the average CPU reaches 70 percent or above the service scales up by one task for each 15 percent increment in CPU utilization up to a maximum of ten tasks, with all logging directed to CloudWatch Logs using a log group name that combines the environment name and the service name.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a security monitoring system for detecting malicious activity in an AWS account by analyzing CloudTrail logs, using a configurable stack prefix parameter defaulting to "sera" and an optional email parameter for alert notifications, where the template imports the CloudTrail log group name and a KMS key ID from another stack via cross-stack references, then creates an SNS topic for security alerts encrypted with the imported KMS key and with a topic policy allowing CloudWatch to publish to it, optionally subscribes the provided email address to that topic, creates CloudWatch metric filters on the imported CloudTrail log group that trigger on specific high-priority events including CloudTrail deletion or logging stoppage (critical severity), IAM role policy modifications and IAM user or access key creation (high severity), security group rule additions (medium severity with a threshold of 5 events), VPC network changes like route creation or internet gateway attachment (high severity), and root account usage (critical severity), with all alarms publishing to the SNS topic and configured to treat missing data as not breaching, and exports the SNS topic ARN and name for cross-stack reference.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a self-contained AWS network backbone designed for hybrid interconnect demonstrations with an OCI primary region, including a VPC, an internet gateway, a private subnet in the first available availability zone, a route table with a default route via the IGW, a transit gateway with a VPC attachment, and a security group that only allows HTTPS inbound from a configurable internal CIDR range and only allows HTTPS outbound to the OCI backbone CIDR; it should also conditionally create a customer gateway and VPN connection to OCI using static routes only, and define a transit gateway route for OCI traffic, all while enabling VPC flow logs encrypted with a customer-managed KMS key that has key rotation enabled and logs stored in CloudWatch with a 30-day retention, and ensuring that all resources use parameterized CIDRs with defaults of 10.94.0.0/16 for the VPC and 10.94.10.0/24 for the subnet.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a self-contained infrastructure for a QuickSight admin console data preparation pipeline, including an S3 bucket with a name incorporating the AWS account ID, an IAM role with permissions to assume roles for Glue and CloudFormation and full access to IAM, QuickSight, Glue, S3, CloudWatch, and Logs, and five AWS Glue jobs written in Python (some using PythonShell with version 3.9 and Glue version 3.0, and two using Glue ETL with Glue version 5.0 and G.1X workers) that load scripts from a predefined S3 location; each job is triggered by a separate scheduled Glue trigger set to run every 3 hours, and the stack must output the S3 paths for group membership, object access, folder assets, folder lookup, folder path, and the cloudtrail log table name and S3 location for downstream use.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a self-contained disaster recovery failover automation stack for a multi-region application. We need a CloudFormation template that creates a new VPC, an ECS cluster, an Application Load Balancer with a security group and an HTTP listener on port 80, a Route 53 hosted zone for dliu.com, and all other resources necessary to deploy the "deweiliu/best-friends" container image as an ECS service using EC2 launch type and bridge network mode, with a desired count of 2 tasks that each reserve 256 MB memory and expose container port 8000 mapped to host port 6000, the service should have a health check grace period of 60 seconds, deployment configuration with maximum percent 200 and minimum healthy percent 50, scheduling strategy REPLICA, and ECS managed tags disabled, the service must be associated with a target group of type instance that uses HTTP on port 80 with health checks enabled, and a listener rule on the ALB with priority 60 that forwards traffic based on the host header bfa.dliu.com to that target group, the template must also provision an SSL certificate in ACM for bfa.dliu.com validated via DNS within the hosted zone, attach that certificate to the ALB listener, create a Route 53 CNAME record with TTL 3600 pointing bfa.dliu.com to the load balancer's DNS name, the task definition must have the family name BestFriendsTaskDefinitionFA22AF8E, a placement constraint requiring x86_64 architecture, the container marked as essential, the log driver set to awslogs with stream prefix best-friends and a CloudWatch log group created with default retention, along with an IAM execution role that has permissions to create log streams and put log events, and a separate IAM task role, and the security group on the ECS cluster must allow inbound TCP traffic on port 6000 from the ALB's security group.
